turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: I do not wish to seem inquisitive, but it is essential to know all the details. Are you aware of the exact location of this house?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Yes, Lady Bracknell, it is indeed essential to know such details. The house at 149 Belgrave Square is where I reside.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Indeed, Mr. Worthing, but what can be the nature of a man who lives in such an address and has no apparent family connections? Can you explain the circumstances surrounding your birth, Mr. Worthing?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I understand your concerns. I was found in a handbag at the railway station in London and have been raised by Mr. Thomas Cardew, who is now the late Algernon's guardian and my guardian as well.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Really, Mr. Worthing, one is surprised and disappointed. Found in a handbag? It is not a fitting origin for a gentleman of your apparent social aspirations. Your birth, however unusual, must be more respectably accounted for.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, I cannot understand your obsession with social standing. Mr. Worthing may not have the pedigree you desire, but he is a man of character and integrity.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, your sentiments are admirable, but as your mother, I must insist on certain standards. Mr. Worthing, the circumstances of one’s birth may be unfortunate, but the manner in which one conducts oneself thereafter is of utmost importance. However, I must reserve judgment until I have further information.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, your skepticism is disappointing. Mr. Worthing is the first man I have ever met who has not been afraid of my outspoken nature.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, I am not unsympathetic to your plight, but it is imperative that we establish a clear and respectable lineage. Your background, while unique, must be thoroughly vetted.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Madam, I understand your concerns and assure you that I am committed to upholding the highest standards of conduct and respectability. I am eager to provide any further information you require to satisfy your inquiries.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, your assurances are noted, but actions speak louder than words. I shall require a detailed account of your life, including any and all connections to persons of questionable character or circumstances.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, I trust you understand the gravity of this situation. Your background must be entirely transparent if you are to be considered a suitable match for my daughter.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Of course, Lady Bracknell. I will provide you with a comprehensive overview of my life and connections, including any details that may be of concern. I am committed to ensuring your satisfaction and Gwendolen's happiness.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: I appreciate your cooperation, Mr. Worthing. Now, let us proceed to discuss your immediate family and any relatives who might cast a shadow on your reputation.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I have no immediate family other than a distant cousin in Hertfordshire. I assure you, there are no relatives who would cast a shadow on my reputation or that of your esteemed family.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, your assurance is noted. However, let us not overlook the possibility of unreported relations or past indiscretions. It is imperative that you leave no stone unturned in this matter.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I understand your concerns and will do everything in my power to address them. I will contact all relevant parties to ensure there are no hidden relatives or past issues that could be detrimental to our discussion.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, it is commendable that you take these matters seriously. However, I must insist on absolute transparency. Should any discrepancies arise, they could jeopardize your standing and, consequently, Gwendolen's happiness.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I promise to be completely transparent and will take all necessary steps to ensure that my background is clear. I value Gwendolen's happiness and my own reputation.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, your commitment is appreciated. However, I must now ask you about your financial situation. It is essential that you can provide Gwendolen with a comfortable life, as her happiness is contingent upon material stability.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: I am engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Pardon me, you are not engaged to any one. When you do become engaged to some one, I, or your father, will inform you of the fact. An engagement should come on a young girl as a surprise, pleasant or unpleasant, as the case may be. It is hardly a matter that she could be allowed to arrange for herself . . . And now I have a few questions to put to you, Mr. Worthing. While I am making these inquiries, you, Gwendolen, will wait for me below in the carriage.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Mamma!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In the carriage, Gwendolen!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Gwendolen, the carriage!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: You can take a seat, Mr. Worthing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Thank you, Lady Bracknell, I prefer standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I feel bound to tell you that you are not down on my list of eligible young men, although I have the same list as the dear Duchess of Bolton has. We work together, in fact. However, I am quite ready to enter your name, should your answers be what a really affectionate mother requires. Do you smoke?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, yes, I must admit I smoke.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am glad to hear it. A man should always have an occupation of some kind. There are far too many idle men in London as it is. How old are you?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A very good age to be married at. I have always been of opinion that a man who desires to get married should know either everything or nothing. Which do you know?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I know nothing, Lady Bracknell.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am pleased to hear it. I do not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance. Ignorance is like a delicate exotic fruit; touch it and the bloom is gone. The whole theory of modern education is radically unsound. Fortunately in England, at any rate, education produces no effect whatsoever. If it did, it would prove a serious danger to the upper classes, and probably lead to acts of violence in Grosvenor Square. What is your income?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In land, or in investments?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: In investments, chiefly.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: That is satisfactory. What between the duties expected of one during one’s lifetime, and the duties exacted from one after one’s death, land has ceased to be either a profit or a pleasure. It gives one position, and prevents one from keeping it up. That’s all that can be said about land.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I have a country house with some land, of course, attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres, I believe; but I dons depend on that for my real income. In fact, as far as I can make out, the poachers are the only people who make anything out of it.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A country house! How many bedrooms? Well, that point can be cleared up afterwards. You have a town house, I hope? A girl with a simple, unspoiled nature, like Gwendolen, could hardly be expected to reside in the country.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, I own a house in Belgrave Square, but it is let by the year to Lady Bloxham. Of course, I can get it back whenever I like, at six months’ notice.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bloxham? I don’t know her.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Oh, she goes about very little. She is a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Ah, nowadays that is no guarantee of respectability of character. What number in Belgrave Square?
